findings.summary: The summary and decision material is spread over all three pages, and new teaching material appears after the part has already been wrapped up.
findings.evidence: Page 1 has 'The Two Models', 'apply vs pop, Final Word' and 'Decision Table'. Page 2 then brings in new material ('Worked Example: Hot Build', 'Worktree Verbs' including `repair`, 'Reading Worktree List') and adds another recap, 'Habits That Prevent Pain'. Page 3 teaches 'Scripting Around The Stack' and then recaps again with 'Two Never-Break Rules' and 'Stash Anatomy Recall'.
findings.fix: Put the order as recipes, then worked examples and worktree verbs, then safe scripting, then one closing recap. Move 'The Two Models', 'apply vs pop, Final Word', 'Decision Table', 'Stash Flags At A Glance', 'Habits That Prevent Pain', 'Two Never-Break Rules', 'Stash Anatomy Recall', the sidebox and the recall callout into a single final section on page 3.

findings.summary: The 'Interrupt, Hotfix, Resume' recipe doesn't give a start point, so the hotfix branch is created from the feature branch's HEAD and would carry unfinished feature commits.
findings.evidence: "git worktree add ../hf -b hotfix-501" — the syntax is `git worktree add [-b <new-branch>] <path> [<commit-ish>]`, and when <commit-ish> is left out the new branch starts at the current HEAD. You run this from the feature tree mid-refactor, so HEAD is the feature branch.
findings.fix: Add an explicit base, e.g. `git worktree add -b hotfix-501 ../hf main` (or `origin/main`), the same way the Hot Build example uses `git worktree add -b fix-88 ../fix main`.

findings.summary: The 'Rescue And Recover' section only covers rescue. The recovery half appears two pages later as bare bullets with no worked commands.
findings.evidence: Page 1 'Rescue And Recover' has only `git stash branch salvage stash@{0}`. Page 3 has 'Dropped entries survive until gc prunes them' and '`git fsck --unreachable` still finds them', with no `git show <sha>` or `git stash apply <sha>` steps.
findings.fix: Add the recovery recipe to page 1 under 'Rescue And Recover': `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` → `git show <sha>` → `git stash apply <sha>`. Then delete the separate bullets from page 3.

findings.summary: The sample `git worktree list` output shows a hotfix worktree that the page only creates in a later block.
findings.evidence: 'Reading Worktree List' shows `/hf    3a71b [hotfix-501]`, but `git worktree add ../hf -b hotfix-501` first appears below it in 'Interrupt, Hotfix, Resume'.
findings.fix: Move 'Interrupt, Hotfix, Resume' above 'Reading Worktree List' so the listed worktree already exists when the reader sees it.

findings.summary: The pushpin on the yellow sticky note covers the end of a comment in the 'Scripting Around The Stack' code block.
findings.evidence: The 📌 icon above the note "one shared stack per repo" sits over the word "pop" in `git stash apply "$sha"  # not pop`, so the last word only partly shows.
findings.fix: Move the sticky note (and its pin) down or right so it sits below the last code line, or add bottom padding to the code block so the pin clears the text of `# not pop`.

findings.summary: The scripting block runs before the page explains why it is needed, and it leaves its entry on the stack without showing how to drop it safely.
findings.evidence: The code block with note 'one shared stack per repo' comes before the bullet that motivates it: '==One `refs/stash`== is shared by every worktree / So a bare `pop` can grab **someone else's** entry'. The script ends at `git stash apply "$sha"  # not pop` with no drop step, even though the same part teaches '`git stash apply` then `drop`'.
findings.fix: Put the shared-stack bullets before the code block. Then add a final step that finds the current `stash@{n}` by "$tag" and runs `git stash drop` on it, since drop takes a stash reference, not a raw SHA.

findings.summary: The page opens with an alias code block that has no heading or setup, so the reader doesn't know what it is for.
findings.evidence: The first block on page 3 is `git config --global alias.sp \ 'stash push -u -m'` with no preceding heading.
findings.fix: Add a heading such as 'Bake In The Safe Defaults' and a line linking it to the 'always -u, always -m' habit. Or move the block right after 'Habits That Prevent Pain'.
